findings.summary: A tailnet login (identified only by the Tailscale-User-Login header) can load /lab, whose page config embeds the server's master token (lab.rs page() passes s.token). The browser then authenticates with the token: XSRF and Origin checks are skipped, a login cookie is set, /mcp is reachable, and removing the login from `allow` does not revoke it. The page must render an empty token for tailnet-identified page loads.

The trust rests on 'the peer is loopback', but any loopback forwarder that passes client headers through (Caddy/nginx, `tailscale serve --tcp` or `funnel --tcp`, `ssh -L`) lets remote clients forge Tailscale-User-Login. security.md frames the risk as only other local processes and does not say the port must be reached only through `tailscale serve`'s HTTP(S) proxy.

notes: First round of six on the tailnet login PR; the class write-up cites it as the clearest 'each fix opened its neighbour' case.
